Question_text: M&R Motors has 2 car showrooms. It buys old cars and repairs them before selling them to its customers. M&R is always trying to increase added value. M&R plans to open another showroom. The owner said: 'Finding the right location is important. The new showroom will require a manager and I need to find someone with the right qualities.' The job will be advertised in the local newspaper as shown in Figure 1. The advertisement will cost $5 for one week.
image: Figure 1 shows a job advertisement for a 'CAR SHOWROOM MANAGER REQUIRED'. The advertisement lists bullet points describing the business expansion, job responsibilities (managing office and selling cars, supervising three car repair workers), required qualities, and offered benefits (good pay and working conditions). It concludes with an instruction to apply to M&R Motors for more information.
Sub_topic: Concept of adding value, increasing added value

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'added value'?
Identify two qualities that M&R might look for in the new manager.
Identify and explain two methods of selection M&R could use when choosing the new manager.
Identify and explain two factors that M&R might consider when deciding on a location for the new showroom.
Do you think a newspaper is the best way for M&R to advertise the new job? Justify your answer.

Question_text: FTT is a social enterprise. It sells its high quality fair-trade coffee beans to retailers in country P. Being ethical is important to FTT. It provides local people with information about micro-finance and skills so they can then start growing beans for FTT to sell for them. FTT wants to start exporting coffee beans as its market research shows increasing demand for coffee in other countries. FTT's managers will have to decide on an appropriate pricing method to use when selling the coffee beans in other countries.

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'social enterprise'?
What is meant by 'micro-finance'?
Identify and explain two factors that might affect the accuracy of FTT's market research.
Identify and explain two ways in which being ethical might help FTT.
Recommend an appropriate pricing method for FTT to use if it starts selling in other countries. Justify your answer.

Question_text: TRB is a small business in the secondary sector. TRB assembles computers. All components, except for the battery and glass for the screen, are imported from other countries. 40% of its products are exported. Many of its competitors are relocating to low cost countries. TRB's Operations Director thinks the opportunities of globalisation may be greater than the threats for TRB. She is looking at ways to improve efficiency in the factory. One option is to introduce lean production methods.

Parts.part_text: TRB is in the secondary sector. Identify the other two classifications of business sector activity.
Identify two ways to measure the size of a business.
Identify and explain two methods of lean production that TRB might use.
Identify and explain two possible benefits to TRB of improving efficiency.
Do you think there are more opportunities than threats from globalisation for TRB? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Bakin Group (BG) is a limited company. It has 3 holiday parks that offer families holiday accommodation and activities. BG aims to look after its customers' needs 24 hours a day. Customers pay for the holidays when they arrive at the park. Each park has 3 managers and 40 part-time employees. BG uses a wide range of social media networks for promotion. The Finance Director is worried about BG's cash flow position. He cannot decide if an overdraft is the best way for BG to solve its cash flow problem.
image: Table 1, titled 'Cash flow forecast for period January - March 2019 ($000)', is presented. It includes data for three months: January, February, and March. Rows detail Cash in, Interest, Wages and other costs, Total cash outflow, Net cash flow, Opening balance, and Closing balance. Specific values are: January (Cash in: 120, Interest: 10, Wages and other costs: 100, Total cash outflow: 110, Net cash flow: X, Opening balance: (40), Closing balance: (30)); February (Cash in: 80, Interest: 10, Wages and other costs: 90, Total cash outflow: 100, Net cash flow: (20), Opening balance: (30), Closing balance: (50)); March (Cash in: 70, Interest: 10, Wages and other costs: 90, Total cash outflow: 100, Net cash flow: (30), Opening balance: (50), Closing balance: Y).
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'limited company'?
Calculate the values of X and Y.
Identify and explain two advantages to BG of having part-time employees.
Identify and explain one advantage and one disadvantage to BG of using social media networks for promotion.
Do you think an overdraft is the best way for BG to solve its cash flow problem? Justify your answer.
